- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp historical spikes, then fail to correct downward.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates when prices are falling, underestimates when rising.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model reacts to recent history but misses medium-term trend shifts.
- When true price drops sharply after a spike, model fails to adjust — continues to forecast higher values.
- Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., below 65) and overestimates in high-price regimes (e.g., above 75).
- Forecasts often ignore recent low-price corrections — fails to recognize “rebound” or “reversion to mean” after sharp declines.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent low prices are not sufficiently weighted in forecasts, leading to persistent overestimation.
